Trumped up treason charges (Zambia)

By: Tarryn Crossman | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We find axactly what happened the night that zambian opposition leader Hakainde Hichilema was brutally arrested on trumped up treason charges.

Summary:
Hakainde Hichilema is the president of the UPND, which is Zambia's biggest opposition party. He is an extremely wealthy businessmen and arrogantly outspoken about his lack of faith in the current ruling party the PF. This outspoken personality has seen him been arrested 15 times since he started running for the 2016 elections in Zambia.
On every previous arrested HH was called to the police station where he would report with his lawyers and challenge the charges legally.

On 10th of April 2017 though nothing happened as it was supposed. 500 armed police officers stormed HH's compound, brutally assaulting and torturing his staff and forcing him, his wife and his child to hide in a secret bunker from 9pm - 10am the following morning. All the while being tear gassed by police, in an attempt to gas them out.
At the gates to the compound UPND MP's were beaten by police and HH's lawyers were denied access.
There was no search warrant and no charges that justified this behaviour. Initially the state tried to charge him with treason based on some defamatory statement he made against president Lung in 2015/2016 but the courts ruled in favour of HH and so the state returned with new treason charges. The bases for this brutality towards HH seems to be an incident that happened a few weeks back. Where HH's motorcade of 60 did not move over for the presidents motorcade, the arrogance of HH seems to have become too much for the ruling party to stand for.
Currently HH's lawyers can see no way for these trumped up treason charges to stand up in court, but treason is an unbeilable offence. So while they fight the state HH will remain behind bars in less than human conditions.
Freedom of speech and police brutality are increasing in Zambia and this case is an extreme example. Two activists were arrested for speaking out in defence of HH on Facebook.
Police's right of reply was denied in a text they sent to me. They will not speak about HH as the matter is in court

1 00:00 Archive footage

V/O -
Devi: during the South African arms struggle Zambia was one of the crucial front line states under the then President Kenneth Kaunda. Who ruled based on the philosophy of humanism, since becoming a multi party state in 1991, Zambia has rounded itself in its democracy, but on the 10th of April this year the current democratic climate was put into question where Hakainde Hichilema or HH the president of Zambia’s major operation party the United Party of National Development was brutally arrested at his home in Zambia and charged with treason.
2 00:34 Interview with Mutinta, HH wife.
Mutinta: it was so terrifying because these were police who were heavily armed, even wearing masks, with guns and other weapons.
3 00:42 V/O: Devi Devi: South Africa’s opposition parties have called for an immediate release of Hichilema, Muleya Mwela is the spokes person for the human right commission in Zambia
4 00:53 Human Rights Commissioner Muleya: From the Human Rights point of view, we have been witnessing the narrowing of the democratic space particular as it pertains to freedom of peaceful assembly and It is in that context that the opposition has been struggling to find that democratic space against the high handedness police action. Well we have been very concerned and have spoken out as a human rights commission. So it’s a political struggle in other words.
5 01:25 V/O Devi: Hakainde Hichilema is a Zambian business and has run as the president of the united party for national development 5 times. With his closes win being in 2016, when he lost to Patriotic Front president the incumbent Edgar Lungu. Hakainde has publicly announced his acceptance Edgar Lungu as the president of Zambia. He was adamant that the elections were rigged and that the UPND were in fact the real winners. He has launched several legal attempts to challenge the elections creating increasing tension in Zambia
6 01:57 Archive footage,
HH speaking HH: this election has been a sham and has not reflected the will of the majority of Zambians. I want him to know he is an illegitimate president.
7 02:08 Devi V/O Devi: on the night of Hakainde Hichilema was arrested, it was unclear what he was being charged with. The state simply attempted to remove him from his home on the middle of the night with no search warrant or warrant of arrest. Martha Mashipe is the Mr Hichilema lawyer, she was forbidden from entering his property, which goes against the Zambia’s constitution.
8 02:28 Interview with Martha the lawyer Martha: They tried to gas him out of house using tear gas. They fished out all his employees and tortured them brutally. We had a battalion of about 600 polices officers who raided his house.
9 02:42 Muleya: We feel torture is absolutely prohibited, under no circumstances should torture take place.
10 02:50 V/O – introduction Mutinta Mutinta is Hakainde wife both her and he 15-year-old son were at the house the night of the arrest.
11 02:55 Interview with Mutinta HH at one time, at some point said “ let me just surrender myself to the police because they are going to kill my people.” I said “ no HH, they are not going to kill those guys, they are not going to kill them its your life that they are looking for’
12 03:11 Human rights commissioner The concern by the general members of the public and the various other stakeholders is the manner in which the Zambia police have been operating. There is a general perception that they are being oppressive that there are allegations of brutality. Now when state agents or security officers, they are getting some past so form of past approval from the powers that be. We don’t how far they can go in violating the rights of citizens

13 04:46 VO – Devi After hiding in with his wife and child in a secret bunker for 12 hours, Hakainde lawyers were given access to his property and he felt safe enough to hand himself over to the Zambian police service. He was place in solitary confinement at a police training campus.
14 04:01 After 48 hours the state must bring that person before a court of law. So in this regard there was the Easter period so they kept him in custody for a period of 6 days before he was brought before the courts of law. That is blatant human rights abuse and it abrogates the provisions of our constitutions
15 04:27 V/O: after Hichilema was initially charged with treason based on defamatory statement he made against the incumbent president Edgar Lungu in 2016, but the court ruled that this charge was bad at law and so the state amended their charge and again indicted Hichilema for treason and this time the charge was based on his motorcade, 60 vehicles not giving way to president Lungu vehicles on route to a tradition ceremony in April 2017
16 04:53 Lawyer So according to what they are saying is that he did not give way or his motorcar should have given way to the presidential motor cared. But there is no law in Zambia, which stipulates that where there is a presidential motor cared you, have to give way.
17 05:14 HR Commissioner Muleya: the charges have been amended twice in an effort for the state to meet the threshold of what constitutes treason. Now it is still subject to judicial enquiry to see if it can actually be sustained as treason
18 05:28 Martha: From a legal perspective I think that there is no offence really or ingredients for the charge ship he is a threat to the incumbent government. And I think that they intend to make sure that they finish him politically.
19 05:47 Mutinita Even me as I'm talking to you now my life is in danger. Even now they are following me
20 05:54 V/O Whether these are trumpet up charges or not treason is a capital offence in Zambia which means that its unbeilable, today Hichilema has been incrassated for over a month and he will remain behind bars until the case is resolved however long that takes
